name: Sena
confidence_why: 3 independent first-hand descriptions agree (2 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.

new_statements.quote: Torrend (1900) observes a tonic accent in Cisena, in general occurring on the penultimate syllable of words. Tonic accents are usually defined as stress realised by an increase in pitch, i.e. these accents are not ‘tones’, but pitch accents. Torrend does not give a definition but states that he only represents the tonic accents in his grammatical description when they deviate from the general pattern on penultimate syllables. No differences in meaning that are expressed by means of tone are described. [p. 79] — Phonologically, Bantu languages are characterised by an open syllable structure (i.e. no consonants in the coda) and tone (typically two distinctive tone levels, i.e. high and low). [...] Tones are not represented in the orthographies of Chichewa, Citumbuka and Cisena. [p. 17]
new_statements.citation: Kiso, Andrea. 2012. Tense and aspect in Chichewa, Citumbuka and Cisena: A description and comparison of the tense-aspect systems in three southeastern Bantu languages. PhD dissertation, Stockholm University.
new_statements.locator: Section 4.3.1 'Tone', subsection 'Earlier findings', printed p. 79 = p. 85; also section 2.2.1 'Phonology', printed p. 17 = p. 23
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (270 pp.) with extracted text. p. 85 carries printed page number 79 and the heading '4.3.1. Tone' / 'Earlier findings' starts on p. 84 (printed 78). The passage is there word for word: 'Torrend (1900) observes a tonic accent in Cisena, in general occurring on the penulti-mate syllable of words. Tonic accents are usually defined as stress realised by an increase in pitch, i.e. these accents are not ‘tones’, but pitch accents. Torrend does not give a definition but states that he only represents the tonic accents in his grammatical descrip-tion when they deviate from the general pattern on penultimate syllables. No differences in meaning that are expressed by means of tone are describe…
new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog penultimate stress (penultimate). The statement is second-hand (a summary of Torrend 1900, which is already the catalog's underlying source type), so it corroborates rather than independently confirms.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word-level 'tonic accent' (a pitch-realised stress) falls on the penultimate syllable of the word as the general rule; Kiso does not analyse Cisena prosody herself but restates Torrend 1900, and adds that no tonal meaning contrasts are described for Cisena and that the orthography does not mark tone.
new_statements.exceptions: Implied only: Torrend marks the accent 'only.. when [it] deviate[s] from the general pattern on penultimate syllables', i.e. non-penultimate accents exist but Kiso lists none.
new_statements.identity_note: Kiso's own Cisena data come mainly from Malawian speakers (Nsanje district) and from the Malawian and Mozambican Bible translations, but her stress statement restates Torrend 1900, which describes the Mozambican (Zambezi) Sena of the Jesuit missions. Funnell 2004 compares the standardised Malawi Sena (MLS) and Mozambique Sena (MZS) varieties. Kiso's bibliography cites the Funnell work as 'Funnell, Barry John (2009).. Ph.D. thesis, University of South Africa', but the UNISA copy (handle 10500/1830) is the September 2004 MA 'dissertation of limited scope' by 'Dr Barry John Funnell', i.e. the same work as the listed 2004 item.

tone_statements.citation: Guérois, Rozenn. 2024. Ideophones in Sena (Bantu, Mozambique). Linguistic Typology at the Crossroads 4(1): 244-288. Bologna: University of Bologna. DOI 10.6092/issn.2785-0943/16685.
tone_statements.quote: As mentioned in §2, Sena does not have tones, but rather stress or accent associated to the penultimate syllable of phrasal domains, and realized through phonetic properties such as loudness and higher pitch. Amidst this predictable stress system, it is interesting to observe that ideophones have a special prosody which makes the distinction between high tones (H), indicated with an acute accent, and zero tones (Ø). The coexistence of stress-like and tone-like properties within the prosodic system of a language is not unique to Sena. It is discussed in detail by Downing (2019) for Tumbuka, a Malawian Bantu language in which tonal contrasts emerge in ideophones only.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 4.3 'Suprasegmental level', p. 257; see also sec. 2, p. 246: 'Unlike most Bantu languages, Sena does not have phonemic tones. It instead shows a rather predictable accentual system associated to the penultimate syllable, similar to that found in Swahili (swh).'
tone_statements.n_tones: None in regular vocabulary (predictable penultimate accent); ideophones contras…

sources.quote: Sec. 24: 'O accento tonico em Sena, quando nao e marcado, acha-se sempre na penultima syllaba. Ex.' / English column: 'The tonic accent in Sena, when not marked in writing, is always laid on the penultimate. Ex. beber kumua=kumua [kúmua] to drink; arvore, pau muti=muti [múti] tree, stick; ribeiro 'nkulo='nkulo ['nkúlo] rivulet.' N.B. on the same page: 'The sounds ua, ue, ui, uo, ia, ie, io, form respectively only one syllable when the u, or i, has no accent.' Sec. 32 (printed p. 17): '1. Formal words always have the tonic accent on the penultimate; informal words may lay the accent on any syllable, as may be seen in the examples above.' (Port.: 'Palavras formadas sempre teem o accento tonico na penultima; palavras informes podem-no ter em qualquer syllaba.')
sources.locator: three-column Portuguese / Chisena / English layout; read from the page scan
sources.note: Core rule matches the catalog (fixed penultimate, penultimate stress). Additions the catalog entry lacks: (a) exception class: 'informal words' (mafala a chipezipezi, 'most of them onomatopoetic, that cannot be analysed' = ideophones, sec. 30, p. 16; examples pópópó 'from all parts', dzólolo 'in a straight line', tápi, jé 'it is pleasing to the taste', mbué 'he arrived') may carry the accent on any syllable; (b) the accent mark is written only 'where there is room for doubt' (sec. 23, pp. 12-13: nsúa 'island', 'nsúa 'mouthful', kusúa 'to peel', kus'ua 'to break'), doubt arising because ua/ue/…

sources.quote: 'The accent in Sena invariably falls on the last syllable but one in a word. In case of a prefix or suffix being added to a word, the addition is treated as part of the word, and the accent shifted accordingly.' óna 'see', onáni 'see ye'. p. 24: with enclitic -nji 'the accent of the verb is then on its last syllable' (mu-na-funá-nji).

sources.quote: As mentioned in §2, Sena does not have tones, but rather stress or accent associated to the penultimate syllable of phrasal domains, and realized through phonetic properties such as loudness and higher pitch. Amidst this predictable stress system, it is interesting to observe that ideophones have a special prosody which makes the distinction between high tones (H), indicated with an acute accent, and zero tones (Ø). The coexistence of stress-like and tone-like properties within the prosodic system of a language is not unique to Sena. It is discussed in detail by Downing (2019) for Tumbuka, a Malawian Bantu language in which tonal contrasts emerge in ideophones only.
